items.claim: A template injection finding is only proved when the response shows the engine evaluating template syntax, not when it shows the payload reflected literally, because a reflection result is explained by ordinary output encoding and proves nothing about the engine.
items.disproof: It IS template injection when a sentinel expression is computed and the computed result appears in the response rather than the expression text; it is NOT when the response contains the payload unchanged, in which case the correct finding is reflected content or XSS at most, and the SSTI claim must be withdrawn.

sources.quote: The Jinja sandbox can be used to render untrusted templates. Access to attributes, method calls, operators, mutating data structures, and string formatting can be intercepted and prohibited.
Twig supports both, automatic escaping is enabled by default.

items.body: Mechanism: A template injection finding is only proved when the response shows the engine evaluating template syntax, not when it shows the payload reflected literally, because a reflection result is explained by ordinary output encoding and proves nothing about the engine. How to apply it in the field: treat this as the fp_rule it is — a hunter must be able to state the concrete observation that demonstrates it, with a request and response in hand, before the finding is reportable. Boundary of the rule: It IS template injection when a sentinel expression is computed and the computed result appears in the response rather than the expression text; it is NOT when the response contains the payload unchanged, in which case the correct finding is reflected content or XSS at most, and the SSTI claim must be withdrawn.

items.claim: The convincing validation pair sends a template expression whose result is a computed value, and the finding stands only when that computed value appears in the response, because a reflected expression could be produced by any endpoint that echoes input.
items.disproof: If the response shows the expression text unchanged or a fixed error mentioning the marker without evaluating it, the proof fails; the pair is convincing only when the returned value is something the server could not have known to echo literally, which is what distinguishes evaluation from reflection.

sources.quote: It is possible to construct a relatively small template that renders to a very large amount of output, which could correspond to a high use of CPU or memory.
The automatic escaping strategy can be configured via the autoescape option and defaults to html .

items.claim: A sandboxed template environment is not a security proof, since the documentation states the sandbox alone is not a solution for perfect security and that resource-exhaustion and side-effecting objects remain outside what it prevents.
items.disproof: It IS effective for the specific primitive it blocks when attribute and method access are genuinely intercepted, which is why a private-attribute probe is rejected; it is NOT sufficient on its own when the attacker reaches resource exhaustion, a passed-in object with side effects, or an output context the template does not understand, and the report must name which of those was actually shown.

sources.quote: The sandbox alone is not a solution for perfect security.

items.claim: Automatic output escaping is an output-context control, not a template-context control, so it prevents an injected value from becoming markup while doing nothing to stop that value from being interpreted as template syntax before rendering.
items.disproof: It does protect the response when the only attacker-controlled surface is a template variable whose value is escaped; it does not protect when the attacker controls the template string itself, because the engine parses that string before any escaping is applied, so the escaping layer is downstream of the compromise.

items.claim: A template engine error message that names the injected payload does not prove the payload was evaluated; a compiler or render error can equally be triggered by malformed template syntax, so error text alone is ambiguous evidence.
items.disproof: It becomes proof when the error is specific to evaluation rather than to parsing, for example a division or type error raised by a syntactically valid expression, which shows the engine executed past parsing; a generic parse error on malformed braces indicates only that the string reached the parser, which is weaker but still real evidence that the template boundary was crossed.

sources.quote: Templates can still raise errors when compiled or rendered. Your code should attempt to catch errors instead of crashing.
What to escape? Any variable that comes from an untrusted source.
